title: Wave Disguise
text: Incidentally, I’d heard in previous loops that Trash was practically under house arrest in the castle. Apparently if he carelessly stepped outside, people would start getting suspicious, so he couldn’t really leave even if he wanted to. That said, in the loop where we headed to Siltvelt, he’d left the castle easily enough. The difference this time is… well, probably a mix of things — the Crimson Swine egging him on, or the burning resentment from letting Father slip away right under his nose. In any case, the current Trash likely only perceives this whole unconfirmed “wave” disaster as something that struck Éclair’s territory, nothing more. Bang! A noble — different from the minister-looking fellow who’d been giving his report earlier — threw open the doors and stormed in.
“How insolent! We’re still in the middle of a meeting!”
“I have no obligation to take orders from the likes of you, who went over our heads to petition King Aultcray with reports that twist the truth!”
Oho? Looks like someone from a rival faction.

“King Aultcray! We’ve received word that the soldiers and nobles sent to aid the disaster victims instead carried out slave hunts against the very people they were meant to rescue! It’s quite possible that Lady Seaetto and her people captured the ones responsible for such an outrage!”
“Don’t go spouting baseless speculation! The truth is we extended a hand of goodwill, and they were the ones who slapped it away!”
“Right! Please see yourself out!” — and with that, the sycophant trying to curry favor with Trash ordered the Éclair-faction noble thrown out of the throne room.

Emotionally, Trash had no desire to cooperate with Éclair’s parent. And yet, he sat there in silence, watching the exchange unfold with an expression that seemed to acknowledge the possibility that the report might be true. No — actually, he sighed, looking distracted, his gaze drifting off toward some far-off point outside.
“Malty……”

And there he goes again, worrying about the Crimson Swine of all things. I suppose the schedule did have her returning sometime soon. He’s praying for her safe return, but let me tell you — that swine is absolutely never coming back! HAHAHA! Anyway, with Éclair’s parent still alive, this exchange seems to be working somewhat in favor of the Éclair faction. Well… as for Trash, I suppose I’ll let this one slide. But with the Three Heroes Church running rampant and being a general nuisance, I’ve become thoroughly convinced that it’d be best to make them behave themselves — just once, good and proper.
Moving from the castle down toward the town below…
“Let us give thanks to the wave for delivering divine punishment upon the demi-humans.”
“Wahahaha! What a joyous occasion!”
“If only it would purify every last inch of demi-human land!”
“Buh-buh-hee!”
“Buh-hee!”

There, in a square, I spotted a crowd leisurely gathered together, spouting these rotten little prayers. What is this? Celebrating a disaster — now that’s what I call rotten to the core. Would even kind-hearted Father and the others forgive this sight? Imagining it, I could picture even their gentle faces furrowing their brows at this.
“I’ve seen news footage of people waving flags to celebrate natural disasters elsewhere before… is it the same everywhere, I wonder? How lamentable.”
I’ve seen garbage like this myself, indeed. If it were Itsuki, wouldn’t he be standing there calculating how to condemn them as evil and abandon them outright?
“As expected of you, O Superior Human-sama. Well said, Motoyasu-san. Itsuki grants his permission, you know.”

And so, as if the Itsuki from the loop where that one riska had taken root chuckled and cheered me on. Being cheered on by Itsuki is rather unwelcome, but isn’t this a fine punishment nonetheless? Quite literally — if the wave destroys an important facility and claims some casualties, surely Melromarc will tighten up its act a little.
And so… to make it quick, so that Éclair’s parent can reach the town below, I’m going to make it look like the wave struck the town too… DEATHZO!

I focused my mind and began chanting the spell, indeed. First, the color of the sky — I’ll apply a variation of Liberation Fireflower to shift it to a hue resembling the wave. I think adjusting the output of Prominence could achieve a similar effect too. Let me reproduce that deep wine-red sky.
“W-what is this!?”
“T-the sky’s turned such a strange color…?”
“I can feel a pressure like magic, but what in the world is this!?”

And so, the people of the town below began to panic at the strange change in the sky. Fuhahahaha! Now then, let me deliver a punishment fitting for that church of theirs, standing there proud as their grand symbol. For a group that smuggled ritual tools for summoning heroes, and on top of that recognized slave-hunting as righteous instead of extending a hand to disaster victims — this is a perfectly fitting reckoning, indeed!

“I, the Love Hunter, command the heavens, command the earth, sever the principles of this world, bind them anew, and purge the corruption. Power of the dragon vein, combine with my magic and the power of the hero — at the command of the Love Hunter, the very source of power. Once more, let all creation be unraveled, and sweep away this foolish mass with a storm of flame!”
“Liberation Firestorm X!”

I unleashed the completed spell straight at the Three Heroes Church. The orb of magic I’d fired — one I’d used before — burst above the church and transformed into a mighty fiery tornado, burning everything around it to cinders! A colossal whirlwind, tall enough to pierce the heavens, swallowed the church of the Three Heroes Church whole.
“T-the church!?”
“W-what is this!?”
“BUHYAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA!?”
I could hear the screams of a pig, but I have no idea what that could be about.
“W-wahhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh!?”
“Why!? What on earth is happening!?”
“Don’t tell me this is the wave!?”
“No way!? Isn’t this supposed to only rain down on demi-humans!?”
“This can’t be happening!”
“Quit messing around with us, you bastard!?”
“GYAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA!?”

And so, cries of utter chaos and despair rang out all around, though of course I have no idea what that could be about. I delivered flames of judgment upon the very people who’d been celebrating Éclair’s territory being struck by disaster like it was some kind of festival! Heroes are objects of worship, so the punishment I deliver is, quite literally, divine punishment — let them take it to heart, indeed!
“Hurry, put out the fire!”
“Gah! What a terrifying blaze!”
“Buh-buhee! Buhiiiiiiii!”
“There are still people inside the church!”
“Hey! Hurry up and put it out!”
“What’s going on!? Isn’t the wave supposed to be judgment that burns away demi-humans!?”
“Daaaaaaaaaaaaaaamn iiiiiiiiiiiit!”

Fuhahaha! Seems there are still a number of people laboring under a misunderstanding. Meanwhile, soldiers and mages from the castle came swarming over, trying to put out the flames, but a spell of mine isn’t going to be extinguished that easily. Well, it’ll burn itself out soon enough anyway. All that’ll be left is the scorched ruins of the church.
“Aaaaah……”

Plenty of people stood there, heads hanging low in despair, but it’s good medicine for them, indeed. And as a bonus, did I manage to take out the pope too, I wonder? In any case, doing this should hopefully make the Three Heroes Church think twice about interfering with Éclair’s parent as well. Mission complete, indeed!
“Hurry, begin the rescue efforts!”

And so, soldiers gathered to clear the rubble of the church and search for survivors, though my spell was nothing on the level of an actual wave, I’ll have you know. Hope they manage to pull through, I suppose. I’ve got no more business here, so let me casually head back over toward Éclair’s side. Honestly… I thought things would settle down peacefully once the wave was over, but what a troublesome bunch they turned out to be, indeed.

Having blown up the church like that, I went to check on Éclair’s parent and the others, only to find… their pace had slowed considerably. On the way there, it hadn’t taken nearly this long, but now they seemed to be advancing cautiously, heightening their guard against the Three Heroes Church. Their pace was slow enough to make me yawn, but if I got too close and seemed to be rushing them, it’d leave an unwanted impression, so keeping watch from a distance was about the best I could manage.
“Fwaaah……”

Even so, I was bored out of my mind. Ahh… here I am, itching to get on with raising my Filolial-sama and all, and instead I have to keep watch over Éclair’s parent’s return to the castle. Just as I was thinking how painfully slow this all was, it seemed they were planning to stay the night at a town along the way.
